identifier_policy.rule: rule_id identifies a recipe family; revision and spec_sha256 identify the registered recipe snapshot. Condition ID is the existing spec item ID. Component IDs are scoped by rule_id/revision/axis/key.
identifier_policy.result: sha256:<full image file SHA-256> identifies a materialized image across paths and datasets. Pending targets have null result IDs. Existing management codes remain the human-readable candidate identifiers.
identifier_policy.scope: Rule IDs are registered here without modifying in-flight specs or historical result records. Resolve condition ID against the registered spec; identical content reuses the same result ID.
identifier_policy.revision: Do not modify a registered snapshot silently. Caption/review changes may change the spec checksum but do not themselves authorize image regeneration; compare actual inference conditions.

training_images.namespace: Input and target images share the result ID namespace sha256:<full image file SHA-256>. Role is a pair relation, not part of image identity.
training_images.pair: items[].id identifies the training pair; it does not require input_result_id and target_result_id to be equal.
training_images.reuse: The same image keeps its result ID across roles, pairs and paths. Reuse the original path or a relative symlink; do not copy image bytes or assign a new image ID.
training_images.lifecycle: Register result IDs after verifying generated file hashes, before admitting a pair to training. Missing outputs have null IDs. Replaced image bytes receive a new result ID while previous generation records remain unchanged.

dataset_composition.target_policy: Simple torso targets reuse the 15 P7-5.2 reference images; separately generated matched targets and their generation feature were deleted.
